findings.title: Avoid rebuilding whole-document metadata on every render
findings.message: With a native listener installed, every render rebuilds the entire document string, rune slice, grapheme boundaries, and line offsets, even when only scrolling or moving the cursor. EditingState and NativeCaretBounds then independently rebuild and scan the document again during notification. This makes visible-only rendering proportional to total document size and introduces substantial allocations and UI latency for large files.
findings.suggestion: Cache the document snapshot, rune data, grapheme boundaries, and line offsets by a document revision, rebuilding them only when the text changes. Reuse that snapshot in EditingState and NativeCaretBounds, and compute positional offsets from the cached line offsets rather than scanning the document repeatedly.
